findings.evidence: `PDF.IsParityInvariant` (Positivity.lean:226-227) is the conjunction of two diagonal equalities; `SpinDensityC.IsParityInvariant` (ComplexSpinDensity.lean:215-217) has those same two as `h.1`/`h.2.1` over ℂ, and `mat_re` (line 162) makes `ρ.re.mat i j = (ρ.mat i j).re`.
findings.fix: Add an unconditional `SpinDensityC.IsParityInvariant.re {ρ} (h : ρ.IsParityInvariant) : PDF.IsParityInvariant ρ.re` (proof: `⟨congrArg Complex.re h.1, congrArg Complex.re h.2.1⟩`), and keep the iff under `h` for the converse, which genuinely needs it.
findings.issue: `isParityInvariant_re_iff` requires `h : ρ.IsTimeReversalInvariant` for the whole iff, but the direction `ρ.IsParityInvariant → PDF.IsParityInvariant ρ.re` is unconditional: applying `Complex.re` to `h.1` and `h.2.1` gives exactly the two real equations. A consumer with parity but not time reversal cannot use the stated lemma.

findings.evidence: Line 291-292: `rw [h1_re, Complex.ext_iff]; exact ⟨Complex.ofReal_re _, by simpa using h.im_transversity.symm⟩` — the hypothesis is consumed only via `im_transversity`.
findings.fix: Restate as `ofReal_h1_re {ρ} (h : ρ.transversity.im = 0) : (PDF.h1 ρ.re : ℂ) = ρ.transversity`, so both `IsTimeReversalInvariant.im_transversity` and `IsParityInvariant.im_transversity` feed it.
findings.issue: `ofReal_h1_re` is stated under `h : ρ.IsTimeReversalInvariant`, but its proof uses only `h.im_transversity : ρ.transversity.im = 0` (line 292). The file itself proves that parity alone also gives that (`IsParityInvariant.im_transversity`, line 248), so a parity-only consumer cannot reach `(PDF.h1 ρ.re : ℂ) = ρ.transversity` through this lemma.

findings.evidence: `mat_toSpinDensityC` (306), `f1_toSpinDensityC` (314), `deltaQ_toSpinDensityC` (318), `transversity_toSpinDensityC` (322), `isParityInvariant_toSpinDensityC_iff` (328) and `re_toSpinDensityC` (335) all carry `@[simp]`; line 310-312 does not.
findings.issue: `isTimeReversalInvariant_toSpinDensityC` is the only `*_toSpinDensityC` lemma without `@[simp]`. Without it `simp` cannot prove `σ.toSpinDensityC.IsTimeReversalInvariant`, so it cannot discharge the side condition of the conditional `@[simp]` lemmas `toSpinDensityC_re` (line 346) and `isParityInvariant_re_iff` (line 354) when the argument is a coerced real density.

summary: The compatibility, exposure and extensionality aspects are clean and the prior round's missing parity eliminator is fixed. Two public lemmas are stated under a stronger hypothesis than their proof uses, and one `*_toSpinDensityC` lemma is missing the `@[simp]` its siblings carry.
